subject: Acme integration: implementation coordinator & SDK migration plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Beth Carter <beth.carter@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - implementation handoff and coordinator (SDK + endpoint migration)

Hi team,

Looping in Marissa (implementation lead) to pick up the technical handoff for Acme. Summary below so everyone has context and an action list. I attached the mutual action plan and a small patch with sample snippets we discussed.

Quick context: Acme is migrating from a hosted endpoint (old-api.acme.ai/v1/generate) to Redwood's hosted API. Expected peak is ~250 reqs/min with many short chat-style interactions (avg 120 tokens in/out). They are planning an initial beta for internal tooling next month.

Top priorities for the next 2 weeks:
- App SDK setup: provide language-specific example + minimal change path for existing HTTP clients. See sample snippets attached (redwood_sdk_samples_v1.patch).
- Endpoint migration: route replacement, header mapping (x-acme-user-id -> x-redwood-user), preserve request_id for troubleshooting.
- Retry & timeouts: recommend idempotency guidance for non-chat calls; for chat streams use short client timeouts + server-side keepalive.
- Rate limit strategy: suggested token-bucket client backoff and exponential jitter for 429s; preserve 429 response body to surface retry-after.
- Monitoring: add a prefix cache for repeated prompts (we discussed a 5000-item LRU) and instrument token-level cost reporting.

Action owners:
- Marissa: target on-call for cutover + run the SDK example validation with Acme staging (action: run SDK test suite and confirm no auth header regressions).
- Monica: own the Mx plan milestone updates in the mutual action plan and coordinate scheduling with Acme.
- Vanessa: I will coordinate executive touchpoints and confirm legal has final T&C redlines before cutover (DocuSign link will be posted in thread).

Key artifacts attached: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_Acme.xlsx, redwood_sdk_samples_v1.patch, pressurized_rate_limit_diagram.png

Quick technical notes to include in handoff (copy into runbook):
- Sample retry window: 250ms -> 1s -> 2s -> 4s (cap 10s) for POST generation calls; 429 -> honor Retry-After if present, otherwise use exponential backoff with full jitter.
- Streaming connections: client keepalive 30s, server heartbeat every 25s on long-lived streams to avoid NAT timeouts.
- Suggested client-side token quotas: soft cap at 10k tokens/min per API key; route to dedicated pool if exceeded.
- SDK change: add an optional "preserve_request_id" boolean to propagate original request ids.

Marissa/Monica — please reply with any missing items or if you want me to introduce any additional folks on the call.

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks Vanessa — picking this up. High-level follow-ups after quick scan of attachments:

1) SDK validation plan (owner: me)
- I will run the patch in Acme staging by tomorrow EOD and validate auth header passthrough + request_id propagation.
- If we see header differences I will add a shim in the Node/Python SDK to rewrite headers with minimal footprint (non-breaking).

2) Endpoint migration checklist (owner: me + Acme eng)
- Confirm Old -> New mapping: old-api.acme.ai/v1/generate -> api.redwood.com/v1/generate (header change + token scope).
- Plan a blue/green cutover: keep old endpoint proxying to Redwood for 48h, switch DNS at low-traffic window.

3) Retries/timeouts (owner: me)
- We'll bake the recommended backoff into the SDK but expose a tunable policy object.
- For streaming chat we will use 35s client-side timeout, server heartbeat 20s (slightly conservative).

4) Rate limit handling (owner: Acme + me)
- I sketched a client-side token-bucket example; attaching a small diagram to the runbook.

Open question for Acme: what is the expected concurrency per API key during beta? That determines batching thresholds and whether we recommend a dedicated pool early.

Scheduling: I can do a 30m deep-dive with Acme tomorrow (Aug 31) at 11:00 PT. Vanessa — can you confirm if legal signoff will land before or after the cutover window so we can plan the DNS switch?

On a related note — I recommend we add a short smoke test in the SDK that runs after deploy (send one sample request, validate 200 + token metrics). I'll paste the test snippet below for quick copy: 

---- sample smoke test (node) ----
const Redwood = require('redwood-sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
(async () => {
  try {
    const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'rw-compact-v1', prompt: 'Hello', max_tokens: 10, preserve_request_id: true });
    console.log('OK', resp.status, resp.token_usage);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Smoke test failed', err.message);
    process.exit(1);
  }
})();
---- end ----

I'll run the test and report results in this thread.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Lead Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference

Answers to your clarifying Qs:

- Short-lived keys: we recommend a fronting token service that exchanges short-lived tokens for a long-lived backend key; we will provide a small reference for rotating keys and we will add a note in the SDK docs with a sample refresh handler.
- Demo: yes — Marissa will walk through the Node + Python snippets and show how the SDK surfaces Retry-After headers and how to tune the retry policy.
